[[File:Nose Myokenzan Nikken.jpg|thumb|200px|right|Statue of Nikken at Nose Myokenzan]]

'''Nikken''' (日乾, 1560 - December 6, 1635) was a Buddhist monk of the {{ill|Nichiren-shū|en|Nichiren-shū|qid=Q206611|lt=Nichiren-shū|1=Nichiren-shū}} sect active during the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|en|Azuchi–Momoyama period|qid=Q319531|lt=Azuchi–Momoyama period|1=Azuchi–Momoyama period}} to the early {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period|1=Edo period}}. He was born in {{ill|Wakasa Province|en|Wakasa Province|qid=Q1053713|lt=Wakasa Province|1=Wakasa Province}} and had the Dharma name "Kōjun" (孝順). He also bore the title "Jakushō-in" (寂照院). Nikken gained the patronage of {{ill|Tokugawa Yorinobu|en|Tokugawa Yorinobu|qid=Q1045763|lt=Tokugawa Yorinobu|1=Tokugawa Yorinobu}}, the lord of {{ill|Kii Province|en|Kii Province|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii Province|1=Kii Province}}'s {{ill|Kishū Domain|en|Kishū Domain|qid=Q1069187|lt=Kishū Domain|1=Kishū Domain}}. With Yorinobu's support, Nikken played a significant role in the revival of [[Rennyō-ji Temple]] (蓮永寺) in {{ill|Suruga Province|en|Suruga Province|qid=Q864170|lt=Suruga Province|1=Suruga Province}}.
